items.title: Japan releases tips on bear spray use amid concern over attacks
items.summary: TOKYO: The Japanese government recently released guidelines on how to check the specifications of bear repellent sprays and properly choose and use them amid a proliferation of ineffective products on the market, Kyodo News reported. With public interest in bear sprays growing as the country faces an increase in bear sightings and attacks, the Environment Ministry and the Consumer Affairs Agency have urged manufacturers and distributors to provide information on the efficacy of their products. "Some products rebranded for bears were actually made for use against people," said Shinjiro Sasaki, a ministry official who also recommended that people practice using the repellents.

items.title: FT mufti: ‘Religious exploitation’ more accurate term, not ‘riding on religion’, to describe misuse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The term ‘religious exploitation’ is more appropriate and objective than ‘riding on religion’ to describe the act of misusing religion for worldly interests, said Federal Territories Mufti Ahmad Fauwaz Fadzil. He said the term ‘riding on religion’ should not be used indiscriminately as it could lead to generalisations about religious figures, including scholars and preachers who sincerely champion the cause of Islam. The term ‘religious exploitation’ focuses more specifically on the act of misusing religion to gain wealth, influence or position, while also more clearly illustrating the existence of those who take advantage and those who are deceived.

items.title: More money for Agriculture Ministry? Anwar says maybe — if the books stay clean, so farmers won’t suffer
items.summary: SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security could receive a bigger allocation in Budget 2027, provided the ministry continues to uphold good governance. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said additional funding could be considered as long as the ministry ensured that public money was managed properly and reached farmers, fishermen and paddy planters. Speaking to reporters later, Mohamad who is better known as Mat Sabu, said the additional allocation is to allow his ministry to prepare early for potential challenges next year.

items.title: At flood-destroyed China-Nepal border, no sign of a once-busy port
items.summary: ABOUT 20 Chinese rescue workers in bright orange operated excavators, shovels and ground-penetrating radar detectors on Sunday in an effort to find hundreds of people missing since a tsunami-like mudslide destroyed China's main border crossing with Nepal. The Gyirong border crossing separating China's Tibet and Nepal became a grisly emblem of the devastation that followed the collapse of a glacier on the Nepal side of the border on Aug 26. Workers had placed a Chinese flag at the spot where the border gate, at nearly 20-meters-tall, once stood.

items.title: Kedah appeals for continued cloud seeding as Pedu, Muda and Ahning dam levels keep falling
items.summary: He said before cloud seeding on Sept 2, total water supply at the Pedu, Muda and Ahning Dams stood at 37.14 per cent, but had dropped to 36.64 per cent this morning. “The water level at Pedu Dam is now at 38.46 per cent, compared to 39.02 per cent on Sept 2, while Muda Dam recorded 9.04 per cent, down from 9.32 per cent previously,” he told Bernama today. Meanwhile, supply at Ahning Dam stood at 45.00 per cent, compared to 45.32 per cent over the same period.

items.title: Police step up highway monitoring as motorists return home after school holidays
items.summary: SLUG: POLHI Police step up highway monitoring as motorists return home after school holidays Austin Camoens austin@nst.com.my KUALA LUMPUR: Police are closely monitoring major highways nationwide as motorists begin making their way home following the school holidays. Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said highway patrol units were on the ground monitoring traffic conditions and ensuring the safety of road users. Hasbullah reminded motorists not to rush despite potentially heavier traffic and longer travelling times.

items.title: Komuniti Madani must be stronger bridge between government and people, says Wan Azizah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Komuniti Madani initiative should play a greater role as a bridge between the government and the people, Bandar Tun Razak member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said. "Do not merely be information transmitters; be attentive listeners to the issues affecting the elderly, families in distress and the needs of the youth," she said at the Komuniti Madani appointment certificate ceremony for the Bandar Tun Razak parliamentary constituency here today. Also present were the Prime Minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Federal Territories Information Department director Normaizatulakmal Tujad, and Bandar Tun Razak Komuniti Madani chairman Jonathan Vela.

items.title: Bukit Lagi Hindu temple row: Perlis police get two more days to detain activist as probe widens into criminal trespass
items.summary: KANGAR, Sept 6 — The remand of a 55-year-old activist detained over social media posts linked to a gathering concerning the demolition of a Hindu temple in Bukit Lagi has been extended by two days as police pursue a separate criminal trespass investigation. Magistrate Ana Rozana Mohd Nor allowed the police application today for the extension, with the activist being investigated under Section 447 of the Penal Code, Harian Metro reported today. Police had said the posts included a picture promoting the Perhimpunan Merah Maha Kali gathering, which was held at the temple site on August 30.

items.title: PPP open to BN-Pas cooperation, but wants to weigh pros and cons
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The People's Progressive Party (PPP) is open to the idea of cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Pas, but wants to assess its pros and cons before taking a position. Its president, Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan, said the party also needed to determine how such cooperation could benefit BN. So, Umno-Pas cooperation is something to do with race and religion.

items.title: Fadhlina pledges no SJKT closures as RM12.6m Sungai Bakap Tamil school project gets going after 17 years
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Sept 6 — The government has assured that no Tamil vernacular school will be closed as construction finally begins on a RM12.6 million replacement building for SJKT Sungai Bakap after nearly 17 years of delays. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the Madani Government would instead continue to focus on the development and maintenance of all SJKT, as well as programmes to strengthen teachers and pupils. “We give an assurance that, under the Madani Government, no SJKT will be closed.

items.title: Firemen put out Klang bush fire amid open-burning surge
items.summary: KLANG: Firemen extinguished a bush fire at Taman Eng Ann here this morning. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 11.05am about the fire in Jalan Murai. "The fire involved a 50ft by 30ft area of bushes.

items.title: 600 Orang Asli youths pursue higher education, triple target set four years ago
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: More than 600 Orang Asli youths are currently pursuing their studies at universities and colleges nationwide, reflecting the government's concern over education issues affecting the community. It was not just 200 entering universities, but more than 300 Orang Asli youths enrolled in universities that year. "Clearly, the achievement of Orang Asli youths entering universities increased to 400 in the second year," he said when officiating the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the EduCity Sports Complex here today.

items.title: OPEC+ set to keep oil output policy unchanged, sources say
items.summary: BENGALURU: OPEC+ is set to keep its oil output policy unchanged for October at a meeting on Sunday, two people familiar with the discussions told Reuters, as the producer group needs to agree on new quotas before deciding its next output steps. In August, OPEC+ agreed to increase production in September, completing a phased rollback of a 1.65 million-barrel-per-day supply cut first agreed in 2023. Before the group decides how to unwind the cuts and return production to the market, it needs to review members' oil production capacity to set 2027 output baselines, which form the basis for quotas.

items.title: Volcanic ash grounds 20 Malaysia-Jakarta flights by Malaysia Airlines, Batik Air
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have cancelled a total of 20 flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today after volcanic ash from the ongoing eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted operations at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport (CGK). Malaysia Airlines said in its post on X that it would cancel 12 flights between Kuala Lumpur (KUL) and Jakarta (CGK), namely MH713, MH712, MH711, MH710, MH717, MH716, MH721, MH720, MH723, MH722, MH725 and MH724. “Further updates on affected flights will be communicated directly to affected customers,” it said.

items.title: Anwar, Al Gore discuss climate crisis, Malaysia's energy transition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim contacted former United States vice-president Al Gore to discuss the global climate crisis and Malaysia's efforts to mitigate its environmental impact. Anwar said they also discussed the haze affecting Malaysia following forest fires in Indonesia. "The discussion also covered Malaysia's commitment and ongoing measures to accelerate the country's energy transition from fossil fuels to cleaner, more sustainable energy sources.

items.title: PPP urges BN to push for early GE16
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional (BN) should push for the 16th general election (GE16) to be held as soon as possible to restore political stability, said the People's Progressive Party (PPP). Its president, Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan, said the country was already experiencing "election fever" following the recent elections in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with the Melaka election expected to be next. Meanwhile, Loga Bala said he hoped the government would consider the higher costs involved in holding state elections separately from the general election.

items.title: M40 group among focus of Budget 2027 initiatives – Finance Minister's aide
items.summary: LUMUT: Budget 2027 is expected to place particular emphasis on efforts to address socioeconomic issues, including the welfare of the middle-income (M40) and lower-income groups, according to an aide of the Finance Minister. Anwar, who is Prime Minister and Finance Minister, is scheduled to table Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on Oct 9. Muhammad Kamil said existing initiatives such as the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) would continue to be strengthened to ease the financial burden on households.

items.title: Zahid: Cloud seeding extended to improve deteriorating air quality in Sarawak
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: The cloud seeding operation was extended across Sarawak to help improve air quality following the haze enveloping several parts of the state. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said two divisions, Kuching and Sri Aman, recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of this morning. Only Kuching recorded a very unhealthy API reading, at 218.

items.title: United Sikhs Malaysia head into Nepal’s worst-hit flood zone to help 98 kids whose parents are missing (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Five Malaysian volunteers are heading deep into one of Nepal’s worst-hit flood zones, travelling over rough terrain to deliver emergency supplies and help families whose homes and communities have been devastated by floods and landslides. The team from United Sikhs Malaysia, a Malaysian humanitarian aid organisation involved in disaster relief and community assistance, is travelling to Dhunche in Rasuwa district to establish a base camp before pushing on to Syapru Besi near the Nepal-Tibet border. https://www.facebook.com/UNITEDSIKHSMALAYSIA/videos/06092026-mission-update-nepal-flood-reliefunited-sikhs-malaysias-team-a-is-curre/3827014714104717/ United Sikhs Malaysia’s mission comes as other Malaysian teams and organisations are also responding to the disaster.

items.title: Women passengers should have option to choose female e-hailing drivers — Loke
items.summary: Women passengers should have option to choose female e-hailing drivers — Loke PUTRAJAYA: E-hailing companies are encouraged to offer female driver options for women passengers to improve their safety and comfort, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke. He said the option would give women passengers an alternative that prioritised their well-being when using e-hailing services. Loke said he had also urged e-hailing companies to introduce women-only carpooling options.

items.title: Cloud seeding extended as Sarawak battles haze
items.summary: KUCHING: Cloud seeding operations across Sarawak have been extended until tomorrow as efforts continue to mitigate transboundary haze affecting the state. Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the extension followed a successful operation yesterday, which brought rainfall to the targeted areas around Bakun and Murum dams. Sarawak has been conducting cloud seeding operations targeting key dams and water catchment areas in the state since Thursday.

items.summary: In the 7am incident, Nur Haira Watikah Mohammad Hamizi suffered severe head and facial injuries after being set upon by five dogs. Her grandmother, Darlinda Darlis, 56, said the toddler was left in her care after her parents left for Johor Baru for work. "After my bath, I looked for Nur Haira and saw the front door open.

items.title: KLIA sets up rest areas for passengers affected by Jakarta airport closure
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has urged passengers travelling to Jakarta on affected flights to contact their airlines for the latest schedule updates after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau forced the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. "At Terminal 1, designated resting areas are at Anjung Tinjau, Level 5 of the Main Terminal Building; the CRS Area, Level 3 of the Main Terminal Building; and Gate C36, Mezzanine Level of the Satellite Building. "At Terminal 2, the resting area is at Level 3A (Mezzanine Floor), Departure Hall," it said.

items.title: No SJKT will be closed, assures Fadhlina
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL: No national-type Tamil school (SJKT) will be closed down, with all such schools continuing to receive support for development, maintenance and programmes to strengthen teachers and students. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the assurance was necessary to address persistent misperceptions within the community that certain SJKTs would be shut down. Fadhlina said the new RM12.6 million school building is vital for the local community and the education of children in the area.

items.title: CJ heads list of 128 Terengganu honours recipients
items.summary: Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Seri Setia Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu (S.S.M.Z), which carries the title Datuk Seri. Tengku Muhammad Ismail also conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Datuk Setia Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu (D.S.M.Z), which carries the title Datuk, on Federal Court judge Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and CelcomDigi Bhd board adviser and former chief executive officer Datuk Mohamad Idham Nawawi. In addition, 27 recipients received the Darjah Kebesaran Datuk Paduka Mahkota Terengganu (D.P.M.T), which also carries the title Datuk.

items.title: Zahid tells parties to park PM talk, focus on Melaka polls instead
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 6 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today urged political parties to put talk of who could become prime minister after the 16th general election aside for now, saying the focus should instead be on the upcoming Melaka state election. The Umno president said it was too early to name or discuss a potential prime ministerial candidate when the timing of Parliament’s dissolution and the next general election remained unknown, Harian Metro reported. Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, said attention should remain on the Melaka election before any discussions on federal-level political matters take place.

items.title: Sarawak extends cloud‑seeding operations to tackle transboundary haze as Serian API shows improving trend
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 6 — Cloud seeding operations across Sarawak have been extended until tomorrow in an ongoing effort to mitigate transboundary haze affecting the state. Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the extension followed a successful operation yesterday, which brought rainfall over the targeted Bakun and Murum Dam areas. Sarawak has been conducting cloud-seeding operations targeting key dams and water catchment areas in the state since Thursday.

items.title: UN must transform into 'UN 2.0' to remain relevant, says Jokowi
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Former Indonesian president Joko Widodo has stressed that the United Nations must reform and redefine its systems, processes and strategies into a new version, "UN 2.0". He said this was necessary to ensure the global institution remains relevant in addressing increasingly complex challenges facing the world. "As we need stronger global institutions, more effective global mediation and more robust global diplomacy to maintain peace, we must now move beyond the old version of the UN and build a new version, UN 2.0.

items.title: Two foreigners remanded for allegedly taking plant specimens without permission from Santubong National Park
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 6 — Two foreign nationals have been remanded for allegedly taking plant specimens without permission from Santubong National Park last Thursday. Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) said both individuals were remanded for three days, from September 4 to September 7, to assist with the investigation. 27], which prohibits the taking or removal of plants from national park areas without permission from the controller of national parks and nature reserves.

items.title: UPTM students to launch companies before graduation under pilot project
items.summary: UPTM pro-chancellor Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the project would be developed with support from Tekun Nasional and Farm Fresh Bhd, which had expressed willingness to help students commercialise their innovations. He was speaking at the First Youth E-Commerce Business Innovation Programme and recognition ceremony for the Malaysia Book of Records title for the "Largest Virtual Participation in an E-Commerce Innovation Platform" here today. The innovation competition featured three themes — Business, Social and Technology — and received 590 project entries involving 2,232 participants.

items.title: Anwar: Issues involving Felda subsidiary to be exposed in coming weeks
items.summary: SERDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said issues involving a subsidiary of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) would be exposed within the next few weeks. "Likewise, in the next few weeks, we will expose the problems involving Felda. Present were Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu and Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.

items.title: MPOB charts new course for palm oil industry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) is shifting into a more market-driven role, seeking to move beyond research and regulation to actively shape the future of Malaysia's palm oil industry. MPOB director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Mohd said the framework marked a fundamental shift in how the agency operates, with greater emphasis on responding to market needs, leading the industry and translating research capabilities into economic value. Badrul said MPOB's research capabilities and technical expertise would also be deployed more strategically to help Malaysia respond to mounting trade challenges.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines, Batik Air cancel 20 Malaysia-Jakarta flights over volcanic ash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have cancelled a total of 20 flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today after volcanic ash from the ongoing eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted operations at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. In a post on X, Malaysia Airlines said that it had cancelled 12 flights between Kuala Lumpur International Airport and Jakarta. Meanwhile, Batik Air said it had cancelled eight scheduled flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today, with six operating between Kuala Lumpur International Airport and Jakarta and two between Subang and Jakarta.

items.title: Investigations into corruption not driven by revenge or jealousy, says Anwar
items.summary: SERDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has rejected claims that ongoing investigations into corruption, abuse of power and misappropriation are driven by revenge or jealousy. Anwar said his role was to ensure the administration of the country operated according to the law, particularly in efforts to curb corruption and abuse of power. Anwar said the government would continue to uphold the rule of law and ensure that enforcement action was taken based on the merits of each case.

items.title: Former minister’s remand extended two days in Tabung Haji RCI hotel‑lease probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The remand of a former minister detained over investigations into a Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) hotel‑lease issue in Saudi Arabia has been extended for two more days. According to Bernama, Magistrate Muhammad Bukhori Md Ruslan Zakariah issued the extension, which runs from tomorrow until Tuesday, after the Malaysian Anti‑Corruption Commission (MACC) applied for it at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court this morning. MACC Chief Commissioner Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak hunt: Reports
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The Pentagon has launched a lie-detector dragnet to comb through high-ranking military officials and identify who leaked information about US munitions stockpiles, according to US press reports. Late Friday, The New York Times reported that some 50 members of the military's Joint Staff – the Pentagon's planning and advisory staff – were being required to take polygraph tests as part of an investigation into how classified stockpile information made its way into journalists' hands. Both outlets cited unnamed officials.

items.title: MAFS budget allocation likely to be increased in line with commendable performance – Anwar
items.summary: SERDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hinted that the allocation for the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (MAFS) is likely to be increased in Budget 2027, in line with the ministry's commendable performance this year. He said the commitment was in line with the ministry's role as a key pillar in ensuring the success of programmes to empower the agricultural sector in the country. Also present were Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu; Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amiruddin Shari; Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar; and MAFS secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak.

items.title: Anwar expresses solidarity with Indonesia over volcanic disaster and haze challenges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed solidarity with the people of Indonesia following the volcanic disaster and haze-related challenges currently facing the country. Anwar said he conveyed this when he contacted former Indonesian President Joko Widodo, better known as Jokowi, who is currently in Penang to attend the Penang Peace Dialogue. In a post on his Facebook page today, Anwar said the conversation also saw the two leaders exchange updates.

items.title: Too early to name PM candidate for GE16, says Zahid
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: It is still too early to name a prime ministerial candidate for the 16th General Election (GE16), says Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. I think we should set that aside for now and focus on the Melaka election," he said. On political cooperation for the Melaka election, he said this would only be decided after the Melaka Legislative Assembly was dissolved.

items.title: Former Skudai rep Marina Ibrahim appointed Johor special officer for Orang Asli
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Former Skudai assemblyman Marina Ibrahim has been appointed Special Officer for the Orang Asli community in Johor under the Sultan Ibrahim Johor Foundation. The foundation is also known as Yayasan Sultan Ibrahim Johor. The appointment was announced by Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi, who spoke as a special representative of the Sultan of Johor, Sultan Ibrahim, to engage with and understand the needs of the state's Orang Asli community.

items.title: Escalating attacks upending daily life in Kyiv
items.summary: COMMUTERS, children rushed underground in the middle of the school day, festivals cancelled, walks punctuated by booming air defences. Near-constant drone attacks are the stark new reality in Kyiv, and daily life is likely to get harder. Kyiv has survived many traumas since Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

items.title: Kedah warns moving Lima could hurt Langkawi's economy
items.summary: ALOR STAR: The Kedah government is concerned that moving the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima) to another state could affect Langkawi's economy, image and standing as an international tourism destination. State Tourism, Culture and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Salleh Saidin said Lima had become deeply intertwined with Langkawi after more than three decades of being held on the island. He said Lima was not merely a defence exhibition but also played a significant role in the local tourism, hospitality, transport, business and economic sectors.

items.title: DOE monitors bush and peatland fires in Mukah, Daro in Sarawak amid dry spell
items.summary: DoE deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said based on the latest status, the fire in the Jalan Sibujaya Barat area had been mostly controlled, covering an area of nine hectares. “However, the fire still affects approximately one hectare in the Jalan Sibujaya Barat area and is currently being extinguished,” she said in a statement on Sunday. Meanwhile, Azuri said two air quality monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am on Sunday.

items.title: Zahid denies rift with Anwar, reaffirms BN’s commitment to political stability
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 6 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied claims of a rift or problems between him and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, stressing instead that Barisan Nasional (BN) remains committed to ensuring the country’s political stability until the end of the term. He said there were no problems, either personally or in official capacity, between him and Anwar, including when attending Cabinet meetings as well as official government functions and events. “I have no problems, either personally or in an official capacity.

items.title: After quitting politics, former Skudai rep Marina Ibrahim is now Johor Sultan’s special officer for Orang Asli affairs
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 6 — Marina Ibrahim, who recently stepped away from politics, is taking on a new role representing the Sultan of Johor in engaging with the state’s Orang Asli community. The former Skudai assemblyman from DAP has been appointed a special officer for Orang Asli affairs under the Sultan Ibrahim Johor Foundation, news outlet Free Malaysia Today reported. Johor Menteri Besar Onn Hafiz Ghazi made the announcement yesterday, saying Marina will work with the community to better understand its needs, while state Agriculture, Agro-based Industry and Rural Development executive councillor Israk Abdullah would also oversee Orang Asli welfare.

items.title: Anwar: MACC to investigate fertiliser‑supply delay to paddy farmers in Kedah; errant contractors may face termination
items.summary: SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to investigate the issue of delays in the supply of Fertiliser 3 to paddy farmers in the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (MADA) area in Kedah. “Do not make farmers and paddy farmers the victims. The delay was reported to have affected about 38,000 paddy farmers cultivating 78,117 hectares of paddy in the MADA area.

items.title: TV volume row leaves woman with slash wound in Kota Tinggi, cops nab husband
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 6 — Police have arrested a Malaysian man in his 70s after he allegedly slashed his wife with a parang during an argument over the TV volume at their house in Taman Desa Sejahtera here. Kota Tinggi police received information at about 9.30pm yesterday about an injured woman bleeding from the wound at home, district police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said in a Facebook statement today. He said a police team was sent to the house where they found the man, who is the victim’s husband, and arrested him.

items.title: KLIA sets up resting areas for Jakarta‑bound passengers after Anak Krakatau ash forces airport shutdown
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 6 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has urged passengers bound for Jakarta on affected flights to contact their airlines for the latest schedule information, after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau forced the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. “At Terminal 1, the designated resting areas are at Anjung Tinjau, Level 5 of the Main Terminal Building; the CRS Area, Level 3 of the Main Terminal Building; and Gate C36, Mezzanine Level of the Satellite Building. “At Terminal 2, the resting area is located at Level 3A (Mezzanine Floor), Departure Hall,” it said.

items.title: Anthony Loke says govt has 15 months to finish reforms, no need to rush GE16
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 6 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today said there is no need to rush into the 16th general election, with the unity government still having 15 months to complete its reform agenda. His remarks came amid calls from several quarters for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to dissolve Parliament early and pave the way for GE16, including from Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said DAP had yet to decide whether to work with BN in the Melaka state election, adding that it was not involved in negotiations between Pakatan Harapan election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.

items.title: DPM Zahid: Over 600 Orang Asli students now pursuing higher education, reflecting rising social mobility
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the achievement was among the outcomes of the government’s emphasis on education as an important instrument to improve the social mobility of the Orang Asli community. The Rural and Regional Development Minister said that when the Department of Orang Asli Development (JAKOA) was placed under his ministry four years ago, an initial target was set for 200 Orang Asli children to gain admission to higher education institutions. Not only did 200 enter university, but the number exceeded 300 Orang Asli who entered university that year.

items.title: PM term limit, AG-PP split: DAP wants both Bills tabled in Oct-Dec sitting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — DAP is pushing for two constitutional reform Bills covering the prime minister’s tenure and the separation of the attorney general and public prosecutor to be brought back to the Dewan Rakyat when its next sitting begins on October 5. DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo said both draft Bills were ready and should be tabled during the sitting, which runs until December 8. According to Gobind, de facto Law and Institutional Reform Minister Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said that the Bills were ready as part of the government’s institutional reform agenda.

items.title: AirAsia cancels, reschedules Jakarta flights as Anak Krakatau erupts
items.summary: In a statement today, AirAsia said volcanic ash posed a significant threat to aircraft safety, prompting operational adjustments to selected services whose flight paths may be affected. “AirAsia has notified all affected guests on their flight status and recovery options,” the airline said, adding that it was working to ensure passengers could resume their journeys safely on the next available flight. The situation remains fluid, and AirAsia urged passengers travelling to and from the affected destinations to check their latest flight status before travelling.

items.title: Construction worker dies in Penang after seven-metre fall at Bayan Lepas site
items.summary: The Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH), in a statement today, said initial investigations found the incident occurred at 1.30 pm, when the victim was descending the scaffolding to take a lunch break. “While descending the scaffolding, the victim fell from a height of about seven metres onto the floor. The investigation is being conducted under Sections 15, 18A and 18B of the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994 (Act 514), as well as the relevant occupational safety and health regulations.

items.title: Varsity student dies, eight in hospital after UiTM endurance challenge in Jengka
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 6 — One participant died while eight others received treatment at hospital after experiencing health problems while taking part in the Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge (KKEC) 2026 at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) in Jengka, Maran. Maran Police chief Supt Wong Kim Wai said police received a report on the incident at 6.59 pm yesterday. Meanwhile, UiTM Pahang branch, in a statement, expressed its profound sadness and extended its condolences to the family of the participant from UiTM Negeri Sembilan branch, the late Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal.

items.title: Malaysia’s SMART team begins Nepal mission after arriving in Kathmandu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) MAS01, which was deployed on a Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission to Nepal, safely arrived at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu at noon local time yesterday. In a statement today, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) said the team completed its arrival procedures and mission protocols by 4.30 pm local time, including logistics clearance and member manifest verification. Malaysia’s SMART MAS01 team in Kathmandu receive a briefing in Kathmandu to assist Nepal with humanitarian aid for the flood disaster on September 6, 2026.

items.title: Breathing isn’t easy in Kuching, Malaysia’s haziest spot at 10am as API hits 223
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur also recorded two areas with unhealthy API readings, while Terengganu, Putrajaya and Labuan each recorded one. In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded an API reading of 163 while Batu Muda recorded 161, while Putrajaya recorded 163. In Pahang, Jerantut recorded an API reading of 168 while Temerloh recorded 164.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim stands by Tuanku Muhriz amid fresh royal succession claim
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 6 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Haji Ismail Lasim today reaffirmed his support and loyalty to Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir amid an ongoing dispute over the state’s royal succession. “Together with the state government, I express my full support and loyalty to His Royal Highness Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan,” he said in a statement on his Facebook page today. Ismail’s statement comes after the Undang Yang Empat, Tunku Besar Tampin and Datuk Shahbandar Sungai Ujong claimed that he had signed a proclamation on August 3 to give effect to the purported removal of Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: US envoy rejects Hadi’s claim it offered to help shape Malaysian govt leadership
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The United States today rejected PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s claim that Washington had offered to help topple Malaysia’s government, saying it has never sought to decide the country’s political leadership. The US Embassy in Malaysia Chargé d’Affaires ad interim David H. Gamble Jr. said any suggestion that the United States had sought to determine Malaysia’s political leadership was untrue. “The United States has never sought to decide Malaysia's political leadership.

items.title: Miri’s landslide-prone roads on Canada Hill set for RM30 million rebuild in 2027
items.summary: “At the moment, we cannot determine what method will ultimately be used to improve the affected sections, including whether the road foundation needs to be reconstructed and the road widened, or whether a bridge structure needs to be built at certain sections. He said should landslides recur after the repairs, the affected sections would have to be dealt with again, underscoring the need for a professional engineering design. However, Lee stressed that immediate action would still be taken to address dangerous sections while awaiting implementation of the RM30 million reconstruction project.
